needs_specification.title: Average-case formula hardness of the majority Andreev function
needs_specification.remaining_issue: With the displayed raw truth-table definition and a uniform distribution on all input bits, a one-leaf formula already has inverse-polynomial advantage. If z is any address with maximal probability \(p_{z}\ge 1/n\), the formula outputting the input table bit \(f(z)\) agrees with \(M_{n}\) with probability \(1/2+p_{z}/2\ge 1/2+1/(2n)\). On a different address the two independent fair table bits agree with probability \(1/2\). Thus the literal inverse-polynomial claim, and the stated \(2^{-o(\log ^{2} n)}\) strengthening, cannot hold for unrestricted De Morgan formulas in this model. A corrected intended target would need a different agreement regime, input distribution, encoding or other source-supported change; none is invented here.

needs_specification.title: Unconditional SAT time lower bounds
needs_specification.remaining_issue: The source paragraph identifies a broad lower-bound program, not one complete benchmark assertion. Choose CNF-SAT versus Circuit-SAT and the encoding/size measure, a particular robust machine model and instruction set, deterministic versus randomized computation, and whether the target excludes linear time, proves a specified superlinear bound, or establishes exponential dependence on the number of variables. These choices cannot be inferred from polynomial-time model equivalence or merged into a single conjunction.

needs_specification.title: Simulation or postselection universality for two-qubit interactions
needs_specification.remaining_issue: The complete source question says “efficiently classically simulable” but does not specify the general easy branch as exact sampling, multiplicative-error sampling with quantified accuracy, or additive-error sampling. Its precise commuting hardness theorem uses pointwise multiplicative error c<√2, which does not fix the easy-branch convention for arbitrary H. In addition, the source quantifies over arbitrary fixed Hermitian H and polynomial-bit time descriptions without a general representation/precision convention for their real constants. A completed benchmark must fix these conventions while preserving the basis-input, restricted-gate and postselection model; this review does not choose a new dichotomy on the source’s behalf.

needs_specification.title: Worst-case hardness behind circuit learning
needs_specification.remaining_issue: The quoted passage leaves two different converse implications open. This card explicitly focuses on efficient learning implying P=NP, while retaining the pseudorandomness alternative as context. The passage describes a randomized learning algorithm but then asks about efficient learning circuits, without fixing uniform versus non-uniform resources for that converse, polynomial resource quantifiers in the target size/error/confidence, or the corresponding uniform complexity conclusion. These choices matter: P=NP, NP contained in BPP, and non-uniform inclusions are different propositions. The full author introduction repeats this wording. Its later precisely parameterized theorem is about provability and does not supply the missing convention for the introductory converse.

needs_specification.title: Direct sums in randomized communication
needs_specification.remaining_issue: The source identifies randomized communication but does not specify total functions versus partial functions or relations, public versus private coins, worst-case versus distributional inputs, global versus per-coordinate error, or the quantitative meaning of a near-perfect direct sum. A recent preprint claims a negative answer for a global-error relation version while explicitly leaving total-function separation open. Select one exact version before treating this as a complete benchmark.

needs_specification.title: Optimal approximation of general-domain k-CSP
needs_specification.remaining_issue: The quantitative approximation scale is recovered, but the source does not select one hardness assumption or one uniformity convention for its optimality claim. Specify whether matching lower bounds should be ordinary NP-hardness, UGC-hardness or an actual algorithmic impossibility under a stated separation, and whether algorithms may depend on fixed arity/domain or must be uniform in both. Randomized expected guarantees also require an appropriate assumption when converted from hardness to impossibility. Do not treat the source’s reversed parameter inequality as the intended regime.

needs_specification.title: Fully dynamic single-source distances beyond rebuilding
needs_specification.remaining_issue: The source passage identifies fully dynamic SSSP and the rebuilding baseline, but does not specify one complete improvement target. Its setting discusses both exact and approximate distances, while the saved sentence does not select the required approximation factor, randomness/adversary guarantees, amortized versus worst-case update cost, preprocessing bound, or a quantified saving and graph-density regime. The paper title cannot supply a deterministic-only restriction for this separate introductory observation. Later work already beats rebuilding for weighted approximate dense instances and exact unweighted dense instances, so the blanket 2017 “nothing better” statement is no longer a current open question. A remaining benchmark must explicitly select the intended unresolved variant instead of silently turning the task into a new all-density deterministic conjecture.

needs_specification.title: Sample-efficient latent-tree Ising learning
needs_specification.remaining_issue: The model and learning output are recoverable, but the requested sample bound is inconsistent across the source passages. The conference question literally asks for \(O(n/\varepsilon^{2})\) samples, while its own Appendix E states an information-theoretic \(\Omega(n\log n/\varepsilon^{2})\) lower bound when the topology is unknown. The July 2023 full author version instead asks broadly about a statistical-computational gap after describing the sample rate up to logarithmic factors. A complete remaining target must select known versus unknown topology and specify whether it asks for the optimal rate up to constants or allows stated logarithmic factors. Do not silently certify the impossible literal unknown-topology bound or substitute a chosen logarithmic allowance.
